The Hist is the great tree our people hold sacred. Its eggs hatch in the pool at its roots. Eleven nights ago its light went out and its leaves shut. The eggs in the pool died. - Nesh-Deeka told me the Hist of Low-Reed Village, the sacred tree of a stilt village east of Lilmoth along the shore, has turned its face. She wants to know whether the cutters who cut the gang's Hist cutting at the burnt camp did this too. I'm to go to Low-Reed Village and speak to Hires-By-The-Season, the root-herald, who speaks for the village to strangers.
- Hires-By-The-Season, the root-herald, told me the Hist of Low-Reed Village shut eleven nights ago and the eggs in its pool died. The village blames the leeches at its roots, and Pays-Late, the tree-minder who keeps the tree. He stands by the roots day and night and will not say why. I'm to get the truth out of Pays-Late, on the bank under the stilts on the south side of the village.
- I threatened to shame Pays-Late before the whole village, and he told me what he hid; he will not forget it. A root of the Hist was cut and its sap drawn off, and the cut was sealed with his own black gum. A boat came in from the north reeds that night. I'm to cross the leech water north of the village to the dry rise past the last stilt house, and take the sap back.
- I took the jars of Low-Reed Village's sap from two men on the dry rise, jars like the one the cutters dropped at the burnt camp: the cutters did this. Pays-Late can pour the sap back at the cut root, or the jars can go to Nesh-Deeka as proof of the cutters' work. I'm to bring them to Pays-Late, by the roots under the stilts, and choose.
- I took the jars of Low-Reed Village's sap from two men on the dry rise, jars like the one the cutters dropped at the burnt camp: the cutters did this. Since I leaned on him, Pays-Late will not trust me to keep his secret. I'm to bring the jars to him, by the roots under the stilts, and choose: back to his tree, or to Nesh-Deeka as proof.
- I gave the jars to Pays-Late on one condition, that he tells Hires-By-The-Season himself that he found the cut and hid it, and he gave his word. He will pour the sap back at the cut root. The cutters drew this tree's sap into jars, as they did at the burnt camp. What do they want with it?
== Helstrom Behind Its Marsh (completed)
- At Low-Reed Village I saw what the cutters do: a Hist cut at the root, its eggs dead and its sap drawn into jars. I'm to tell Nesh-Deeka at Salts-The-Catch's house in Lilmoth what I found.
- Nesh-Deeka told me a Hist that falls silent kills no eggs, but a cut Hist does, and the villages of the interior must learn the difference. The tree-minders and the Nisswo, the wandering priests who read the Hist, meet at Helstrom behind the marsh. She wants them to hear it from someone the Reed can deny, so I go alone and do not name the Reed. I'm to take the coast ship from Lilmoth's stop and go ashore by its door to Helstrom's river landing.
- I came ashore at Helstrom's river landing. The way in is root and shallows, where Nesh-Deeka says two giant wasps keep the far bend. In the grove just inside the city's gate stand Ei-Tuja, a Nisswo who reads for anyone, and Kaska-Meen, a tree-minder who hears few strangers. I'm to tell Ei-Tuja what I saw at Low-Reed Village, or ask him whether Kaska-Meen will hear it.
- I told Ei-Tuja what I saw at Low-Reed Village, and he will preach it openly in every village he walks to. He told me what a dying Hist leaves: a Mnemic Egg, a seed of its sap holding its memories, once used to stop a generation of eggs hatching. Is that what the cutters are gathering sap for?
